cards.explanation: The answer is Canaanites, friends. God says, "Your origin and your birth were in the land of the Canaanites." That's where God starts Jerusalem's story. He goes all the way back to the very beginning. Then He says her father was an Amorite and her mother a Hittite (Ezekiel 16:3).

The answer is not a single one, friends. Zero. No cord cut, no washing, no salt rub, no cloths. God says no one cared enough to do even one of these things out of compassion. That's a whole list of care, and she got none of it.

The answer is True. God says she was "…thrown out into the open field, because you were despised on the day of your birth." That's a heavy beginning for anybody. I think this is where the story hurts most.
The answer is that He tells her to live, friends. God says, "…as you lay there in your blood I said to you, 'Live!'…" Then He says it again. He sees her in the worst spot and speaks life over her.
The answer is False. She's grown and very beautiful, but God says she was "…naked and bare." The fine clothes don't show up until verse 10. First comes the cloak.

The answer is that He enters into a covenant with her, friends. God says, "I pledged Myself to you, entered into a covenant with you, and you became Mine…" It's a promise, and He's the one making it. She goes from the open field to belonging to Him.

The answer is a beautiful crown, friends. God says, "I put a ring in your nose, earrings on your ears, and a beautiful crown upon your head." He keeps adding to the outfit. Meanwhile all I've got on my head is a tall white hat, and I'm proud of that hat.
The answer is False. God says, "Your fame spread among the nations on account of your beauty…" It was no secret. The word got out far past her own front door.

The answer is the splendor God gave her, friends. God says her beauty "…was perfect in the splendor I bestowed on you…" It was a gift from Him. Keep that in your pocket, friends, because it matters for what comes next.
The answer is True. God says, "…because of your fame, you trusted in your beauty…" Her trust landed on her beauty. That's the turn in the story, friends.

The answer is idols, friends. God says, "You also took the fine jewelry of gold and silver I had given you, and you made male idols with which to prostitute yourself." The gold and silver came from God's hands, and she used it to make idols. That's a heavy verse.

The answer is True. God says, "…you set before them as a pleasing aroma the food I had given you…" That food was the fine flour, oil and honey He had fed her. Then He adds, "That is what happened…" Even her meals went to the idols.

The answer is the days when she lay in her blood, friends. God says, "…you did not remember the days of your youth when you were naked and bare, wallowing in your own blood." She forgot where she came from. Forgetting her beginnings is a big part of this story.

The answer is False. God says she "…built yourself a mound and made yourself a lofty shrine in every public square." She built them at the head of every street too. These were out in the open for everyone to see.
The answer is the Egyptians, friends. God says, "You prostituted yourself with your lustful neighbors, the Egyptians…" They're the first neighbor He names.
The answer is False. God says the daughters of the Philistines "…were ashamed of your lewd conduct." These are people who hated her, and even they were ashamed. That tells you how far it went.

The answer is that she is still not satisfied, friends. God says, "…you were not yet satisfied. Even after that, you were still not satisfied." That's the Assyrians, after Egypt. She keeps reaching and keeps coming up empty.

The answer is that she pays her lovers to come to her, friends. God says, "…you gave gifts to all your lovers. You bribed them to come to you from everywhere…" Then He says she paid a fee instead of receiving one. He calls it the opposite of other women.

The answer is the blood of her children, friends. God says it's "…because of the blood of your children which you gave to them…" This is one of the heaviest parts of the whole passage. I think this one hurts.

The answer is all of her lovers, friends. God says, "…I will surely gather all the lovers with whom you found pleasure, all those you loved and all those you hated." He gathers them from all around. The ones she turned to become the ones standing against her.
The answer is True. God says, "…I will sentence you to the punishment of women who commit adultery and those who shed blood…" Both are named. This is a heavy verse.

The answer is that they'll tear them down, friends. God says her lovers "…will level your mounds and tear down your lofty shrines." The mounds are leveled and the lofty shrines are torn down. What she built up is what comes down.
The answer is False. God says they will "…execute judgment against you in the sight of many women." It's done where people can see.

The answer is pay, friends. God says, "I will put an end to your prostitution, and you will never again pay your lovers." Back in verse 34, He says, "…you paid a fee instead of receiving one…" That paying is what God says will never happen again.

The answer is False, and that's good to hear. God says, "So I will lay to rest My wrath against you, and My jealousy will turn away from you. Then I will be calm and no longer angry." The anger is laid to rest. After a passage this heavy, that's a relief.
